policy.note: Direct dependencies only. Transitive dependencies inherit approval from their allowlisted direct parent and are deliberately not filed. See README.md for what that does and does not protect against.

npm.identityNote: An npm package's only manifest-visible owner is its scope. Registry `maintainers` is mutable metadata that a consumer never declares, so it is not a checkable identity. Unscoped packages therefore cannot be approved by author and must be listed one at a time.

@types.reason: DefinitelyTyped. Type declarations only -- no runtime code reaches a consumer's bundle, and every stub comes from one repository under one review process.

freshness.why: A single stub's publish date is not a maintenance signal for DefinitelyTyped; the repository is the project. @types/marked-terminal last published 2025-08-03 and that says something about marked-terminal, not about DT.

@tanstack.reason: TanStack. One organisation, one release process; react-query, react-table and react-virtual are all load-bearing in fancy-query and fancy-grid.

@testing-library.reason: Testing Library. Test-only, never shipped, and the suite's TDD rule depends on it.

@tailwindcss.reason: Tailwind CSS v4 ships its integrations as @tailwindcss/* packages. react-fancy is built on Tailwind v4; the framework and its integrations are one project.

react.reason: The UI framework the whole suite is built on. React 19 only since kit 0.5.

react-dom.reason: React's DOM renderer. Inseparable from react.

typescript.reason: The language every TS package is written in.

typescript-eslint.reason: TypeScript support for ESLint; the rules-of-hooks lint runs on it.

eslint.reason: The suite's linter, wired into all React repos after the rules-of-hooks sweep found two live crashes.

vitest.reason: The TypeScript test runner named in the TDD rule.

jsdom.reason: DOM environment for vitest component tests.

tsup.reason: The build tool for most TypeScript packages in the suite.

freshness.why: Last npm publish was 2025-11-12, but the repository is committed to. Development attention has shifted toward tsdown (which fancy-tui already builds with); if the next re-verification finds no commits, the answer is migrating rather than renewing.

tsup.review: Last RELEASE was 2025-11-12 (280 days). Alive on commits only. Decide whether the suite migrates to tsdown before this override expires 2026-11-19.

tsdown.reason: Rolldown-based bundler; fancy-tui's build tool and the likely successor to tsup across the suite.

tsx.reason: TypeScript execution for build and generator scripts.

vite.reason: The dev server and bundler for every app and for fancy-pwa's peer surface.

laravel-vite-plugin.reason: Vite integration for Laravel apps; part of the Laravel toolchain.

@vitejs/plugin-react.reason: React support for Vite. Maintained by the Vite team.

concurrently.reason: Runs the dev processes side by side in app scaffolds.

tailwindcss.reason: The styling system react-fancy is built on; a peer dependency of every UI package.

clsx.reason: Conditional className joining. Runtime dependency of react-fancy, fancy-whiteboard and fancy-flow.
clsx.review: FAILS THE FRESHNESS BAR. Last release 2025-06-27, last commit 2024-06-10 (lukeed/clsx). Feature-complete and 234 bytes -- the honest options are to vendor the ~20 lines into fancy-file-commons or react-fancy and drop the dependency, or record an owner decision to accept an unmaintained one. It is a runtime dependency shipped to every consumer, so this is the highest-value item on this list.

tailwind-merge.reason: Resolves conflicting Tailwind classes; runtime dependency of react-fancy's class merging.

marked.reason: Markdown parsing in react-fancy and fancy-tui.

zod.reason: Schema validation for fancy-flow node configuration and typed llm_call output.

zustand.reason: The store fancy-screens exposes as a peer for cross-screen presence.

ulid.review: FAILS THE FRESHNESS BAR. Last release 2025-11-30, last commit 2026-02-27 (ulid/javascript, 173 days). ULID is a frozen spec and the implementation is small; vendoring it or moving to crypto.randomUUID where ordering is not needed both remove the dependency outright.

axios.reason: The HTTP client Laravel and Inertia scaffolds ship with; peer of classroom and job-board.

@inertiajs/react.reason: Inertia.js. The integration seam fancy-inertia and fancy-query exist to serve.

laravel-echo.reason: Laravel broadcasting client; the transport behind fancy-query's live invalidation.

pusher-js.reason: The websocket client Laravel Echo drives, including against Reverb.

composer.identityNote: Every Packagist name is vendor/package and Packagist enforces vendor ownership at registration, so the vendor prefix is a genuine, checkable owner identity -- the strongest of the three ecosystems.

laravel.reason: The framework the PHP side of the suite is built on. Anything Laravel publishes is in scope by construction.

illuminate.reason: Laravel's read-only component splits. Same project, same releases, different package names.

symfony.reason: Laravel is built on Symfony components; symfony/process and symfony/yaml come from the same foundation we already depend on.

pestphp.reason: Pest. The PHP test runner named in the suite's TDD rule.

phpunit/phpunit.reason: Pest runs on PHPUnit; several packages target it directly.

orchestra/testbench.reason: Laravel package testing harness. The only way to feature-test a Laravel package outside an app.

mockery/mockery.reason: Test doubles for PHP; part of the standard Laravel test stack.

nunomaduro/collision.reason: CLI error reporting in the Laravel test stack.

nesbot/carbon.reason: Date handling. Effectively part of Laravel and required directly by laravel-fms.

guzzlehttp/guzzle.reason: The HTTP client behind the fancy-git provider adapters and Laravel's HTTP facade.

inertiajs/inertia-laravel.reason: The server half of Inertia; the seam fancy-seo and fancy-inertia are built around.

spatie/browsershot.reason: Headless-Chrome rendering for the showcase's PDF and image capture.

fakerphp/faker.reason: Test and seed data across the Laravel packages.
fakerphp/faker.review: FAILS THE FRESHNESS BAR. Last release 2026-02-04, last commit 2026-05-02 (FakerPHP/Faker, 109 days). Marginal and widely relied upon -- it arrives transitively with orchestra/testbench anyway, so the cheapest correct fix in most repos is dropping the direct require-dev entry and letting it be inherited.

http-interop/http-factory-guzzle.reason: PSR-17 factory bridge required by knplabs/github-api and php-gitlab-api.
http-interop/http-factory-guzzle.review: FAILS THE FRESHNESS BAR. Last release and last commit both 2025-12-15 (246 days). It is a thin PSR-17 adapter; php-http/guzzle7-adapter or a locally-written factory would remove it. Both fancy-git-github-php and fancy-git-gitlab-php require it directly.

pypi.identityNote: PyPI has no namespace at all -- a requirement string carries no owner, and project ownership is not derivable from what a consumer declares. Author-level approval is therefore NOT EXPRESSIBLE for Python, and every distribution is listed individually. This is a real difference between registries, not an oversight.

pytest.reason: The Python test runner for the -py mirror packages.

ruff.reason: Linter and formatter for the Python packages.

mypy.reason: Static type checking for the Python packages.

packageGrants._note: A grant approves a library FOR ONE PACKAGE, because that package exists to wrap or host it. It does not approve the library anywhere else. Keys are the manifest name (package.json name / composer.json name / [project] name), falling back to the repo directory name for manifests that declare none.

echarts.reason: The charting library this package exists to wrap. Peer, never bundled.

echarts-gl.reason: ECharts' GL renderer, for the 3D chart types the wrapper exposes.

leaflet.reason: The OSM map engine this package exists to wrap.

freshness.why: Last npm publish 2025-08-16, but the repository is actively committed to. Leaflet's release cadence is slow by design; the commit stream is the live signal.

@googlemaps/js-api-loader.reason: The Google Maps engine adapter's loader. Google's own package.

@xterm/xterm.reason: The terminal emulator <Terminal> exists to wrap. Peer, never bundled.

@xterm/addon-fit.reason: xterm.js' own resize addon; required for the controlled sizing contract.

three.reason: The engine this adapter exists to wrap. Peer, so the consumer owns the version.

@babylonjs/core.reason: The engine this adapter exists to wrap. Peer, so the consumer owns the version.

@simplewebauthn/server.reason: The WebAuthn server implementation this package wraps. We write no cryptography of our own.

@simplewebauthn/browser.reason: The browser ceremony helper the passkey UI drives. We write no cryptography of our own.

freshness.why: Last npm publish for the browser package was 2026-03-10; the monorepo it lives in is actively committed to and its server sibling published 2026-06-24.

web-auth/webauthn-lib.reason: The WebAuthn implementation the PHP side wraps. We write no cryptography of our own.

spomky-labs/cbor-php.reason: CBOR encoding, required to build WebAuthn attestation fixtures in the test suite.

@xyflow/react.reason: React Flow. The canvas the optional FlowEditor is built on -- the headless /engine entrypoint never imports it.

ai.reason: The Vercel AI SDK, behind the opt-in ./llm/vercel-ai adapter only. Core declares registerLlmClient and imports no provider SDK.

@dagrejs/dagre.reason: Graph auto-layout for the editor's tidy-up action. Editor-only, dev dependency.

stripe.reason: The Stripe SDK this package exists to wrap. Peer, so the consumer owns the version.

stripe/stripe-php.reason: The Stripe SDK this package exists to wrap. Version ceiling is set by laravel/cashier, not by us.

stripe.reason: The Stripe SDK the Python catalog mirror wraps. Optional extra.

octokit.reason: GitHub's own SDK; the library this provider adapter exists to wrap.

freshness.why: The `octokit` meta-package last published 2025-10-31 while its component packages and repository move constantly. The meta-package's publish date understates the project's activity.

knplabs/github-api.reason: The GitHub API client this provider adapter wraps.

http-interop/http-factory-guzzle.reason: PSR-17 factories required by knplabs/github-api. See the package entry -- it fails the freshness bar.

@gitbeaker/rest.reason: The GitLab API client this provider adapter wraps.

m4tthumphrey/php-gitlab-api.reason: The GitLab API client this provider adapter wraps.
m4tthumphrey/php-gitlab-api.review: FAILS THE FRESHNESS BAR. Last release and last commit both 2026-05-06 (GitLabPHP/Client, 105 days). Marginally over. Single-vendor client with a small maintainer team -- re-check before the next release of fancy-git-gitlab-php; if it stays quiet the adapter should talk to the REST API through guzzle directly, which it nearly does already.

http-interop/http-factory-guzzle.reason: PSR-17 factories required by php-gitlab-api. See the package entry -- it fails the freshness bar.

node-pty.reason: Microsoft's pseudo-terminal bindings. The OS primitive this backend exists to expose; there is no pure-JS equivalent.

ink.reason: The React renderer for terminals that fancy-tui's components are built for. Peer, so the consumer owns the version.

chalk.reason: Terminal colour. Runtime dependency of the ANSI rendering path.

string-width.reason: Correct display width for wide and combining characters; the layout is wrong without it.

marked-terminal.reason: Renders markdown to ANSI for the TUI's Markdown surface.
marked-terminal.review: FAILS THE FRESHNESS BAR. Last release 2025-01-28, last commit 2025-09-02 (mikaelbr/marked-terminal, 351 days). It is a marked renderer -- fancy-tui already depends on marked directly and already owns its own ANSI code path, so absorbing the renderer is a real option rather than a rewrite.

ink-testing-library.reason: Renders Ink components in tests; the fancy-tui suite is written against it.
ink-testing-library.review: FAILS THE FRESHNESS BAR, WORST IN THE TREE. Last release 2024-05-22, last commit 2024-06-28 (vadimdemedes/ink-testing-library, 782 days). Test-only, so nothing ships to consumers, but the suite's own showcase harness already renders real Ink output -- that harness is the replacement.

simple-icons.reason: The brand-mark source this pack is generated from. Build-time only; the published package ships generated paths, not the dependency.

pa-ux-sandbox._reason: The showcase installs the PEER dependency of every wrapper it demonstrates. Those peers are approved for the wrapper that owns them; the host needs its own grant to install them, and listing them here keeps that explicit rather than promoting them to blanket approvals. Keyed on the REMOTE name (Particle-Academy/pa-ux-sandbox), not the envelope path repos/px-ui-sandbox -- the remote name is the identity that is the same here and in Actions.

echarts.reason: Peer of fancy-echarts, which the showcase demonstrates.

echarts-gl.reason: Peer of fancy-echarts, which the showcase demonstrates.

leaflet.reason: Peer of fancy-map, which the showcase demonstrates.

freshness.why: Same finding as the fancy-map grant: alive on commits, slow on releases.

@googlemaps/js-api-loader.reason: Peer of fancy-map's Google engine adapter.

freshness.why: Same finding as the fancy-passkeys-ui grant.

ink.reason: Peer of fancy-tui; the docs site renders real Ink output for the TUI previews.

ink-testing-library.reason: Drives the Ink render harness that captures the fancy-tui docs previews.
ink-testing-library.review: FAILS THE FRESHNESS BAR (last commit 2024-06-28). Same finding as the fancy-tui grant.

puppeteer.reason: The browser spatie/browsershot drives for PDF and social-card capture.

react-router.reason: Routing for the standalone preview surfaces that render outside the Inertia page tree.
react-router.review: The app routes with Inertia. A second router is either load-bearing for the preview iframes or a leftover -- confirm which, and drop it if it is the latter. Fresh (2026-08-18), so this is a fitness question, not a maintenance one.

@tsrx/vite-plugin-react.reason: Vite plugin for Ripple TS (.tsrx modules), used by the experimental Ripple demo route.
@tsrx/vite-plugin-react.review: WOULD NOT HAVE BEEN APPROVED AS-IS. Version 0.0.x from a pre-1.0 framework (Ripple-TS/ripple), and the sandbox pins ^0.0.21 while upstream is at 0.0.93 -- a caret on 0.0.x pins the exact version, so this has been frozen 72 releases back since the day it was added. Fresh (2026-08-17) and MIT, so the bar it fails is fitness, not maintenance: decide whether an experimental framework belongs in the showcase host at all, and if it does, unpin it.

stripe/stripe-php.reason: Required directly by the showcase's checkout routes alongside laravel-catalog.

fancy-starter-kit._reason: A Laravel application scaffold. Its dependencies are the app stack a fresh `laravel new` receives, not library dependencies.

lightweight-charts.reason: The charting engine this package exists to wrap. Optional peer, never bundled. Chosen over echarts on measured evidence: echarts has no update-in-place API for a candlestick series, so a tick costs 18.45ms against 2.36ms on a realistic two-pane trading chart, at 3.6x the bundle. See .ai/plans/fancy-trading.md section 1.
lightweight-charts.review: ATTRIBUTION IS OWED, AND IT IS INHERITED BY OUR CONSUMERS. Apache-2.0 with a NOTICE that npm does NOT ship. Every commercial consumer of a fancy-chart built on this must display either the on-chart attributionLogo (which defaults to true -- pass it through, never silently false) or the NOTICE text plus a link to https://www.tradingview.com/ on a user-facing page. The exact bytes to reproduce are in .ai/knowledge/lightweight-charts-attribution.md; copy them, do not retype -- the (c) in the NOTICE is Cyrillic U+0441, so grep '(c)' will not find it. Not legal advice.
